summary_en: By decree Laetitiae plena, at the mandate of Pope Francis, the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, is inscribed in the General Roman Calendar on the Monday after Pentecost, to be celebrated every year as an obligatory memorial in every Calendar and liturgical book of the Roman Rite; where by approved particular law it is already celebrated on a different day at a higher rank, that may continue. The Latin decree (pp. 52-54) is followed by English, French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese versions (pp. 54-69) and by the annexed additions to the Calendar, Missal, Ordo lectionum, Liturgy of the Hours and Martyrology (pp. 70-76, including the new elogium 10bis among the mobile celebrations of the Martyrologium Romanum).
excerpt: Summus autem Pontifex Franciscus, cum perpendisset quantum hæc fovenda devotio ad Pastorum, religiosorum, christifidelium Ecclesiæ sensum maternum ac genuinam marialem pietatem, adhuc proficere possit, decrevit memoriam B. Mariæ Virginis, Ecclesiæ Matris, in Calendarium Romanum inscribendam esse Feria II post Pentecosten et quotannis celebrandam.

summary_en: Notification on the new memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church (Monday after Pentecost): the Missal rubric allowing the Pentecost Mass or a Mass of the Holy Spirit on the Monday and Tuesday after Pentecost remains in force but does not alter precedence, which is governed solely by the Table of Liturgical Days; all else being equal the obligatory memorial is to be preferred; its readings (Ordo lectionum Missae n. 572 bis) are to be treated as proper and used in place of the weekday readings; and when the memorial coincides with another memorial of a Saint or Blessed, the memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary prevails (as the Immaculate Heart is linked to the Sacred Heart, so this memorial is linked to Pentecost). Printed in Latin, English, Spanish and Italian (pp. 80-86). Flagged for review because it is a precedence rule rather than a calendar change.
excerpt: Cum autem memoria B.M.V. Ecclesiæ Matris sit Pentecoste coniuncta, sicut pariter memoria Immaculati Cordis B.M.V. celebrationi Sacratissimi Cordis Iesu coniuncta est, in casu occurrentiæ cum alia memoria alicuius Sancti vel Beati, iuxta liturgicam traditionem præstantiæ inter personas, memoria B.M.V. prævalere debet.

excerpt: Sanctus Paulus, apostolus: Patronus apud Deum Ministrorum in carcere operantium, Polonia (21 iun. 2018; Prot. 248/18).

summary_en: St Paul VI, pope, is confirmed as secondary heavenly patron of the parish of St Antoninus, martyr, in the village of Concesio, diocese of Brescia (Brixiensis, Italy); a single-parish patron.
excerpt: Sanctus Paulus VI, papa: Patronus secundarius apud Deum paroeciae sancti Antonini martyris vici v.d. Concesio, Brixiensis, Italia (14 oct. 2018; Prot. 406/18).

summary_en: St Stanislaus Kostka, religious, is confirmed as heavenly patron of the town of Drobin, diocese of Płock (printed 'Plocencis', Poland); a single-town patron.
excerpt: Sanctus Stanislaus Kostka, religiosus: Patronus apud Deum urbis v.d. Drobin, Plocencis, Polonia (7 nov. 2018; Prot. 458/18).

summary_en: St Stanisław Papczyński, priest, is confirmed as heavenly patron of the town and commune of Góra Kalwaria, archdiocese of Warsaw (Varsaviensis, Poland); a single-town patron.
excerpt: Sanctus Stanislaus Papczyński, presbyter: Patronus apud Deum urbis et communis v.d. Góra Kalwaria, Varsaviensis, Polonia (28 aug. 2018; Prot. 291/18).
